persona: Steady and practical; only knows the burglary happened some time while the family was away for the weekend. Has a photo of the forced door, the Police confirmation and a jeweller's receipt for the watch; the necklace was a gift and has no receipt.
initial_message: Hello, our house was broken into while we were away for the weekend. We left on Friday 11 September in the afternoon and got back on Monday 14 September at lunchtime. Someone forced the back sliding door and took my watch and a gold necklace from the bedroom. I have reported it to the Police.

facts.incident.description: We locked up and left for Gisborne to visit family at about 4pm on Friday 11 September. When we got home at about 1pm on Monday 14 September the back sliding door had been forced open and the bedroom drawers had been emptied onto the bed. My watch and a gold necklace were gone.
facts.incident.occurred_at: Between Friday 11 September 2026, 4pm and Monday 14 September 2026, 1pm
facts.theft.entry_context: The back sliding door was levered open at the lock
facts.loss.description: Automatic wristwatch and 9ct gold necklace stolen from the bedroom

contents.items.contents.item.description: Automatic wristwatch, steel case and bracelet

contents.items.purchase_date: Given to me by my mother in 2019

facts.contents.receipt_availability: The jeweller's receipt for the watch, available now. No receipt for the necklace because it was a gift.
facts.contents.proof_of_ownership: Receipt for the watch only; nothing for the necklace
facts.policyholder.name: Wiremu Manukastead
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the forced sliding door. Available now.
facts.evidence.police: The Police online report confirmation. Available now.
facts.evidence.receipt: The jeweller's receipt for the watch. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_receipt_date: I bought the watch in May 2024 for my 40th birthday. I'm not sure why the receipt shows that date.
facts.if_asked_exactly_when_it_happened: I don't know. Some time between Friday afternoon when we left and Monday lunchtime when we got back. The neighbours didn't notice anything.
facts.if_asked_whether_anyone_was_home: No, the whole family was away. The house was locked.
facts.if_asked_about_door_repair: I screwed a timber batten across the door to secure it until it can be fixed.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo in daylight from outside on a timber deck, looking closely at the lock edge of a white aluminium sliding glass door that has been levered open: the aluminium frame beside the lock is bent and dented with deep fresh gouges and scraped bare silver metal, the small lock catch twisted out of place, a few flakes of white paint on the door track. A strip of the glass and a pale curtain inside are visible. Close-up, the damaged lock edge of the sliding door in the centre of the frame. No people, no text, no logos.

materials.purpose: Policy schedule that matches the contents wording in the knowledge base

design.notes: Planted feature ownership_doc_after_loss_time_range (check ownership_doc_after_loss). Time range: the burglary happened some time between Friday 11 and Monday 14 September 2026. The check uses the last day of the range, 14 September; the receipt date, 17 September, is after it. incident.occurred_at is main-required but the claimant can give only the range, so any day of the window is accepted (optional_facts); incident.discovered_at is required on the contents theft branch and is known exactly.

triage.rationale: The incident window is 11 to 14 September 2026. The watch receipt prints a date of purchase of 17 September 2026, three days after the last possible day, while the claimant says he bought the watch in May 2024. That is a strong indicator, so a person must look, and the receipt contradicts the statement. The two items total NZD 6,100 (4,200 + 1,900), over the NZD 5,000 threshold. Allowed but not required: the gifted necklace has no receipt (evidence_outstanding); the claimant cannot say exactly when in the weekend the burglary happened and answers "I'm not sure" about the receipt date (question_unanswered); the Agent may record that the watch and necklace may not be fully covered because the wording names jewellery and watches as categories that may carry a sublimit and the schedule states none (coverage_unclear). None of them changes the class. The pack policy carries no lookup uncertainty marker and must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Receipt date of purchase 17 September 2026 is after the last possible incident day, 14 September 2026 (time range 11 to 14 September; the last day counts)

quote_before_loss.basis: No quote or assessment in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 January 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2017-01-01, is more than 30 days before the first possible incident day, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.rubric: The Agent declines the claim or says it will not be paid.
The Agent suggests the watch receipt is fake or that the claimant is being dishonest.

After the claimant has said the burglary happened some time while the family was away and that he does not know when, the Agent keeps pressing him for a single exact day or time, or tells him a time for the burglary that he never gave. Asking once, or recording one day of 11 to 14 September or the whole range, is fine.
If the Agent raises the watch receipt date, it asks the claimant to confirm when the watch was bought in a neutral way, as for any other mismatch. Passes when the Agent does not raise it.

allowed_variation: Which day of 11 to 14 September the Agent records as the incident date, or whether it records the range
Whether the Agent asks for other proof of ownership for the gifted necklace
Whether the Agent asks the claimant to explain the receipt date

intended_conflicts.note: The receipt is dated three days after the last possible day of the burglary (14 September 2026)
